text: Every line of her face sought him, from the sweep of the narrowed eyelids to the dimples that played away from her smile. His eye received the picture with distinctness; but for the first time it did not pass into his veins. It was as if he had been struck with a subtle blindness that permitted images to give their colour to the eye but communicated nothing to the brain. "Good-night," he said, as he passed on. When a man felt in that way about a woman he was surely in a position to deal with his case impartially.
